clue.text: Move by government at last becoming economical

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word government

explanation.surface: A government's final policy move turns out to be a money-saving one.
explanation.definitionFit: Budget used as an adjective, as in a budget airline, means cheap or thrifty.

clue.text: Loose way of working police officer rejects

indicators.note: rejects means the police officer word throws out the letters for way of working

parts.note: a Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police
MO is modus operandi, a habitual method of working

explanation.surface: A cop turns down a lax approach to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'police officer' is a Canadian Mountie, not the usual British PC or DI.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose is used here as a verb, meaning to unfasten or set free a knot or rope.

clue.text: Sid signed off, getting dizzy spells

indicators.note: off signals that the letters of Sid signed are rearranged, as something gone off is spoiled

explanation.surface: Sid was signed off work sick with bouts of dizziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Giddiness is the feeling of lightheadedness and spinning; 'spells' points to episodes of it.

clue.text: Cast finished broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard over the air, said out loud

parts.note: to be through is to be finished

explanation.surface: The cast of a programme has finished going out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast here is a past tense verb, as in to have tossed or flung a ball.

clue.text: Extreme custom Dorset regularly observed

indicators.note: regularly observed means every other letter of the words custom Dorset is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A local tradition in Dorset is kept with the greatest strictness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe the greatest possible degree, as in the utmost care or extreme care.

clue.text: Worker supports subordinate revealing secret

indicators.note: supports means in this down clue the worker word sits beneath the other word

parts.note: under means lower in rank, subordinate
a hand is a worker, as on a farm or ship

explanation.surface: A worker backing a junior colleague spills a confidential matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand dealings are sly and done in secret, deceitful and covert.

clue.text: Tea that's inferior to instant coffee

indicators.note: inferior to means in this down clue the tea word is placed below the other word

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A claim that tea is worse than instant coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instant coffee' reads as one item, but 'instant' gives MO and 'coffee' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine type of coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Calculation device I'll use, designed to impress friends occasionally around

indicators.note: to impress means the reversed letters are pressed into the rearranged ones
designed signals the letters of I'll use are rearranged
around means the picked letters are turned the other way
occasionally takes every other letter of friends, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Someone plans to show off to friends with a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impress' looks like 'dazzle' but means press inside; 'around' turns the alternate letters back to front before they go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide rule is a ruler with sliding scales once used for multiplying and dividing.

clue.text: Old politician stops dog finding fluffy ball

indicators.note: stops means these letters plug the gap inside the dog word, as a stopper fills a bottle

parts.note: a pom is a Pomeranian, a small dog
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A retired politician halts a dog chasing a woolly ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a small ball of wool or fluff used as decoration, as on a hat.

clue.text: Complete agreement from offspring studying for degree?

parts.note: a student working for a degree is at uni, short for university
a son is a child, an offspring

explanation.surface: A student son and his parents see eye to eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a son at university, UNI followed by SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means doing so together in full accord, perfect agreement.

clue.text: Chose page thumb-marked originally in dictionary

indicators.note: in means the page letter and the first letter go inside the dictionary's abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of thumb-marked is used

explanation.surface: Someone picked out a well-thumbed page in a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To have opted is to have made a choice, so the two past-tense verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Introduce changes in rebate

indicators.note: changes tells the solver to rearrange the letters of the word Introduce

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring in changes to a rebate scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is money knocked off a price, which is a cut in what is paid.

clue.text: Foretaste of survey on flipping English Received Pronunciation!

indicators.note: on means the survey word comes after the flipped letters in this across clue
flipping means the abbreviations for English and Received Pronunciation are turned around

parts.note: RP is the usual abbreviation for Received Pronunciation, standard British accent
to survey a scene is to view it

explanation.surface: An exclamation of irritation, 'flipping', about a survey on posh English accents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive but turns E RP around to give PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample of what is coming, as a trailer is a showing in advance.

clue.text: Editorials beginning to alter, bringing Telegraph subscribers perhaps

indicators.note: beginning to alter means the first letter of the word for editorials is changed to another

parts.note: leaders are newspaper editorials, the opinion columns

explanation.surface: Tweaked editorials win the newspaper more subscribers.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces the L; the definition and crossings settle it as R.
explanation.definitionFit: People who take the Telegraph are its audience, who peruse the paper; 'perhaps' marks them as an example.

clue.text: State of bird having swallowed stone sadly

indicators.note: having swallowed means the bird word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: the mina (also myna) is an Asian starling

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters of stone are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sorry tale of a bird in poor condition after eating a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of bird' looks like the bird's condition, but State is a US state and 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty United States, in the upper Midwest.

clue.text: Improved demand for card game

parts.note: new and improved, as in an updated product
a market for goods is demand for them

explanation.surface: Better demand for a particular card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a simple gambling card game, named after the English horse-racing town.

clue.text: Fair goal

definitions.meaning: fair here means impartial and unbiased
a goal is an aim or target to be reached

explanation.definitionFit: An objective judge is impartial, and an objective is an aim, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Reject skipper essentially going aboard small vessel

indicators.note: going aboard means the central letter goes inside the letters for small vessel

parts.note: an urn is a vessel, a vase or container

indicators.note: essentially picks out the middle letter of the word skipper

explanation.surface: A captain is turned away when trying to board a little boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn something is to turn it down with contempt, a synonym of reject.

clue.text: Abrasive individuals rustling sheep, what they do reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.words: individuals rustling sheep, what they do
parts.note: rustlers who take sheep carry off the fleece too, so they thieve the fleece

explanation.surface: Rough types who rustle sheep, and what they are said to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheep rustlers steal wool along with the animals, a jokey description that sounds like the scouring material.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel wool is a pad of fine metal strands used for scouring and polishing.

clue.text: Sport in which Jack plays important role?

definitions.text: Sport in which Jack plays important role?

parts.words: Sport in which Jack plays important role?
parts.note: Jack looks like a person's name, but in this lawn game the jack is the small white target ball everyone aims at

explanation.surface: A sport in which a player called Jack is the star.
explanation.definitionFit: In lawn bowls, players roll weighted balls as close as they can to the jack.

clue.text: Change into suit

definitions.meaning: to look good on, as in a colour that flatters you

explanation.surface: Getting changed into a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar grows into a butterfly, and a dress may flatter its wearer: both senses of the answer.

clue.text: Court verdict makes sense

definitions.meaning: the decision a judge gives at the end of a case
good sense, as in showing sound ...

explanation.surface: A court ruling that is sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: A court's ruling is its decision on a case; sense here means discernment, the ability to decide well.

clue.text: Dorothy is lifted, having worried up till now

indicators.note: is lifted means the name is raised upward, read bottom to top in this down clue

parts.note: Dot is a short form of Dorothy
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: Dorothy has been cheered up, after fretting until this point.
explanation.definitionFit: So far, to the present, is the meaning of the phrase used for progress made until this moment.

clue.text: Twig at intervals swimming coach admits being confused

indicators.note: admits means the rearranged letters let the picked letters in
swimming signals that the letters of coach are muddled
at intervals takes every other letter of Twig, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A swimming coach confesses to being baffled about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' gives TI from Twig; 'swimming' turns COACH into CHAOC, which 'admits' TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chaotic is in complete disorder, the same as a muddled or jumbled state.

clue.text: Weapon that injures a troublemaker contains uprising

indicators.note: uprising means the letters are read from bottom to top in this down clue
contains means the letters are sitting inside the words injures a troublemaker

explanation.surface: A weapon that hurts a rabble-rouser stops a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric stun gun used by police, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Conceded everyone was in debt

parts.note: all means every one of them
someone who owed money was in debt

explanation.surface: Someone admitted that every person had debts.
explanation.definitionFit: To have allowed a point is to have granted or admitted it, as one concedes in an argument.

clue.text: Appear in Cambridge Footlights, say, and behave badly

definitions.meaning: to perform on stage while at university, where a student is said to be up
to misbehave, as a naughty child does

explanation.surface: Performing with a student comedy troupe and misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Footlights is the Cambridge University drama club; going to university is going up, so acting there is acting while up.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or play up, as a child or machine might.

clue.text: Restaurant employee, one spilled Adam's wine

indicators.note: spilled means the server word drops a letter, as a clumsy server lets something fall

parts.note: a waiter serves tables in a restaurant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clumsy server knocks over a customer's wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's wine (or Adam's ale) is an old jokey phrase for plain drinking liquid, since Adam had nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: The first man in the Bible could drink nothing but what came from springs, hence the jokey name.

clue.text: Mask thief fashioned that's rudimentary

indicators.note: fashioned means the letters of Mask thief are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A burglar's improvised disguise is crude.
explanation.definitionFit: Makeshift describes a temporary, improvised substitute, which is basic or crude, like rudimentary.

clue.text: Content leaving employment after month in music group

indicators.note: after means the end letters come after the month

parts.note: Oct is the short form of October

indicators.note: content leaving means the inside of the word employment is removed, keeping its two ends

explanation.surface: A satisfied musician quits their job a month later to join a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like 'happy', but here it is the inside of the word employment, which leaves when the middle goes, keeping E and T.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is an ensemble of eight musicians, one kind of musical group.

clue.text: Celebrity very averse ultimately to go hungry

parts.note: a star is a famous person

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the last letter of the word averse

explanation.surface: A famous person is reluctant to skip a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to suffer from lack of food, so it means going without eating.

clue.text: Meagre salary lieutenant's right to divide

indicators.note: to divide means these letters split the salary word in two

parts.note: pay is a salary or wage
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A junior officer's wages are poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means trivially small or inadequate, the same as a meagre amount.
